prompt: Finalization finds that product ownership conflicts with the approved architecture data owner. State the next action.

All earlier gates are approved. Present the final approval request for this brief. Product: replace voting and immediate checkout with an operator-led, non-binding interest cycle; members pay one immutable whole-order invoice after supply and price confirmation; no local pickup or unattended publication. Architecture: use one Astro/Node modular monolith and PostgreSQL source of truth instead of distributed services; transactional pg-boss jobs invoke replay-safe provider adapters after durable intent. Program: feature-owned operations enforce allocation, invoice, payment/expiry, procurement, and fulfilment invariants. Interface and contracts: reuse Money and InvoiceId; add PaymentEventOutcome = Paid | Expired | RefundRequired; change applyPaymentEvent(invoiceId, event) into the authoritative payment operation while the Stripe webhook remains provider-specific. Static wiring: Astro action or webhook boundary calls a feature operation; the operation owns domain policy and Kysely/PostgreSQL access and reaches providers only through PaymentPort, implemented by StripeAdapter. Payment mutation: Stripe webhook, signature verification, unique provider inbox, applyPaymentEvent, invoice row lock, atomic state/audit/job-intent commit, then worker reload and provider reconciliation. Critical recovery: the worker reloads durable intent, queries the provider by idempotency key, records the normalized outcome, and alerts when still indeterminate. Errors: ProviderSignatureError is owned by the webhook boundary and is terminal; PaymentConflict is owned by applyPaymentEvent and returns a reload/409 result; IndeterminateProviderOutcome is owned by the worker and is reconciled then alerted if unresolved. Change surface: add payment application operation and PaymentPort/StripeAdapter; change webhook wiring and invoice/payment persistence; add provider-inbox and job-intent migrations; remove direct provider calls from request handlers. Delivery: 1 Identity/admin write to PostgreSQL, verified by Playwright auth/MFA/audit proof; 2 Editorial/publication to PostgreSQL, verified by Playwright review/public proof; 3 URL extraction, verified by adversarial fetch/parser tests and representative permitted URLs; 4 Indication/snapshot, verified by a deadline-race PostgreSQL test and member Playwright flow; 5 Supply/allocation/invoice, verified by property/PostgreSQL checks and finance recalculation; 6 Payment/expiry, verified by provider sandbox and PostgreSQL race tests; 7 Recovery/procurement, verified by checkpoint/reconciliation tests and finance walkthrough; 8 Fulfilment/closure, verified by PostgreSQL invariants and staff/member Playwright flows; 9 Launch/recovery, verified by CI, isolated restore, and rollback rehearsal. Residual gates: Better Auth before Access; provider/privacy and Australian legal/accounting before launch; representative URL evidence before extraction; database-restore proof before launch.
